concepts.title: Reproductive Health, RCH Programmes and Awareness
concepts.definition: Reproductive health covers complete well-being in every dimension of reproduction -- physical, emotional, behavioural and social -- and India pursued it socially through family planning from 1951 and later the RCH reproductive and child health initiatives, awareness drives, school sex education and a law forbidding amniocentesis when used to pick the foetus's sex.
concepts.key_idea: Education that busts myths, plus medical support for pregnancy, delivery and contraception, is the backbone of a reproductively healthy society.
concepts.textbook_ref: lebo103.txt lines 1-101 (reproductive health problems and strategies section)
question_patterns: what does the WHO idea of reproductive health include beyond healthy organs
name the action plans India launched to build a reproductively healthy society
why should sex education be introduced in schools
what is amniocentesis and why is its use for sex determination banned
which indicators show that a society's reproductive health is improving
list the problems an RCH programme offers medical assistance for

solution_steps.explain: Beyond normally working reproductive organs, the WHO view adds emotional, behavioural and social well-being in all sex-related matters.
Family planning began in 1951 and widened into RCH programmes: awareness through media, parents and teachers, plus facilities for pregnancy, delivery, STIs, contraception and infertility care.

Amniocentesis -- sampling amniotic fluid to read fetal cells for disorders like Down syndrome or sickle-cell anaemia -- is statutorily banned for sex determination to curb female foeticide, and child immunisation is promoted.
Falling maternal and infant mortality, more medically assisted deliveries, wider birth-control choice, Saheli developed by CDRI Lucknow, and more small families all signal improvement.

concepts.title: Population Explosion and Growth-Rate Projection
concepts.definition: Better health services cut death rates, maternal mortality and infant mortality so sharply that world numbers swelled from about 2 billion in 1900 to 7.2 billion by 2011; at an annual growth rate of r, a population of size P grows to P times (1 plus r) raised to the number of years.
concepts.key_idea: Smaller-family motivation, raised marriage ages and contraceptive access are the counter-measures to growth that scarcity of food, shelter and clothing cannot absorb.
concepts.textbook_ref: lebo103.txt lines 102-132 (population stabilisation passage and 2011 census rate)
question_patterns: project a country's population several years ahead from its annual growth rate
work out what a billion-strong population becomes after a few years at 2 percent yearly growth
which factors are blamed for the population explosion of the last century
why does a growth rate near 2 percent still alarm planners
what steps has the government taken to motivate smaller families
at what legal ages can women and men now marry and how does that check population

solution_steps.explain: A growth rate expressed per year converts to a multiplier by adding one to the rate.
Each year multiplies the population by the same factor, so the effect compounds exponentially.
The compounded figure is the expected population after the given span.

worked_examples.question: Using Population Explosion and Growth-Rate Projection, compute the result for annual_growth = 3, current_population = 3, years = 3.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: Build the yearly growth factor: growth_factor = 1 + annual_growth = 4.0 Step 2: Compound it over the years: projected_population = current_population * growth_factor ** years = 192.0 Step 3: Read off the projection: result = projected_population = 192.0 Final result: 192.0

worked_examples.question: Using Population Explosion and Growth-Rate Projection, compute the result for annual_growth = 4, current_population = 4, years = 4.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: Build the yearly growth factor: growth_factor = 1 + annual_growth = 5.0 Step 2: Compound it over the years: projected_population = current_population * growth_factor ** years = 2500.0 Step 3: Read off the projection: result = projected_population = 2500.0 Final result: 2500.0

compute_steps.action: substitute the given values into the formula

concepts.title: Natural and Barrier Contraceptive Methods
concepts.definition: Device-free tactics -- periodic abstinence over the fertile window of days 10 to 17, withdrawal before ejaculation, and lactational amenorrhea up to six months postpartum -- sidestep gamete meeting, while rubber barriers such as condoms, diaphragms, cervical caps and vaults block it physically, often backed by spermicidal creams.
concepts.key_idea: Condoms double as STI and AIDS shields, natural methods carry almost no side effects but fail often, and reusable female barriers are paired with spermicides.
question_patterns: which days of the menstrual cycle form the fertile period for periodic abstinence
how does the lactational amenorrhea method work and how long is it dependable
name the barrier devices available for men and for women
why are condoms recommended beyond their contraceptive role
what is coitus interruptus and what limits it
why are spermicidal creams applied along with diaphragms and cervical caps

solution_steps.explain: Abstain from coitus around days 10-17 when ovulation is due, withdraw before ejaculation, or rely on intense breastfeeding to suppress ovulation for at most six months after childbirth.
No drugs or devices means near-zero side effects, but failure chances run high.
Male or female condoms (Nirodh is a classic male brand) stop semen entering the tract and also guard against STIs and AIDS; diaphragms, cervical caps and vaults cover the cervix and are reusable.
Creams, jellies and foams applied with the female barriers raise their contraceptive efficiency.

concepts.title: Intra Uterine Devices and Their Modes of Action
concepts.definition: IUDs placed in the uterus through the vagina come in three families -- non-medicated loops like Lippes loop, copper-releasing CuT, Cu7 and Multiload 375, and hormone-releasing Progestasert or LNG-20 -- raising sperm phagocytosis, and with copper ions damping sperm motility and fertilising power, while hormone types additionally harden the uterus against implantation.
concepts.key_idea: IUDs suit women who want to delay or space pregnancies and rank among India's most accepted contraceptives.
question_patterns: classify intra uterine devices into their three types with one example of each
how do copper ions released by an IUD disable sperms
what extra effect do hormone releasing IUDs produce in the uterus and cervix
why are IUDs advised for women who wish to delay or space childbirth
who inserts an IUD and by which route
name the non medicated IUD example mentioned in your text

solution_steps.explain: Non-medicated (Lippes loop), copper-releasing (CuT, Cu7, Multiload 375) and hormone-releasing (Progestasert, LNG-20) types all sit inside the uterus, fitted by doctors or trained nurses.
All IUDs step up phagocytosis of sperms within the uterus.
Released copper ions suppress sperm motility and their fertilising capacity.
Hormone types make the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervical mucus hostile to sperms, completing the contraceptive cover.

concepts.title: Oral Pills, Injectables, Implants and Emergency Contraception
concepts.definition: Daily progestogen or progestogen-estrogen tablets taken for 21 of every 28 days block ovulation and implantation and thicken cervical mucus; the same hormones run in longer-acting injections and skin implants, and any of these plus IUDs used within 72 hours of coitus serve as emergency contraception.
concepts.key_idea: Saheli, a once-a-week non-steroidal pill from CDRI, shows how oral contraception can cut dosing and side effects while staying effective.
concepts.textbook_ref: lebo103.txt lines 203-223 (pills, Saheli, injectables, implants, emergency contraceptives)
question_patterns: describe the daily schedule and action of contraceptive pills
how do oral pills interfere with ovulation and with sperm entry
what makes Saheli different from ordinary steroidal pills
how do injectables and implants differ from pills in duration of effect
within how many hours must emergency contraceptives be taken after coitus
what traits should an ideal contraceptive show

solution_steps.explain: Small daily doses start within the first five days of the cycle, run 21 days, pause for the 7-day menstruation gap, then repeat; they inhibit ovulation and implantation and alter cervical mucus to slow sperms.
Progestogen alone or with oestrogen also comes as injections or sub-skin implants acting much like pills but lasting far longer; Saheli is a weekly, non-steroidal alternative.
Progestogen-estrogen combinations or IUDs given within 72 hours of unprotected or forced intercourse can avert an unwanted pregnancy.

A good contraceptive is user-friendly, easily available, effective, reversible, near side-effect-free and leaves sexual drive and the act untouched; possible troubles like nausea, breakthrough bleeding or irregular cycles still deserve attention.

concepts.title: Sterilisation: Vasectomy and Tubectomy
concepts.definition: Surgical sterilisation is the terminal contraceptive route: a snippet of the vas deferens is cut or tied through a scrotal incision in a vasectomy, or of the fallopian tube through the abdomen or vagina in a tubectomy, stopping gamete transport in either sex.
concepts.key_idea: Both operations are highly effective yet very hard to reverse, so they suit partners who want no further pregnancies.
question_patterns: compare vasectomy and tubectomy in site and procedure
why are surgical methods called terminal contraception
through which incision is each sterilisation operation performed
what exactly is blocked in the male and female surgical methods
why is reversibility poor after sterilisation
who should consider sterilisation as a contraceptive choice

solution_steps.explain: Surgery blocks the gamete highway rather than touching hormone levels, and is advised as a final step once family size is complete.
In vasectomy a small length of the vas deferens is removed or tied through a tiny scrotal cut, so sperms never reach the urethra.
In tubectomy a short piece of the fallopian tube is removed or tied via an abdominal or vaginal route, so the ovum cannot meet sperms.
Both are near foolproof but reversal is very poor, so counselling and a settled family decision should precede them.

concepts.title: Medical Termination of Pregnancy: Safety and Law
concepts.definition: MTP is the deliberate ending of a pregnancy before full term -- safest in the first twelve weeks and riskier in the second trimester -- legal in India since 1971 with conditions, and governed by the 2017 amendment act on how many registered doctors must certify each case.
concepts.key_idea: Roughly 45 to 50 million MTPs worldwide each year equal about a fifth of conceptions, and misuse for female foeticide is precisely what the law is built to stop.
concepts.textbook_ref: lebo103.txt lines 253-329 (MTP section and amendment act box)
question_patterns: up to how many weeks is a medical termination considered relatively safe
on what grounds does Indian law permit a pregnancy to be terminated
how many registered medical practitioners must agree for a termination between twelve and twenty four weeks
why was the MTP Act amended and what did it aim to reduce
list the situations in which an MTP becomes medically necessary
how does misuse of MTP connect with female foeticide in India

solution_steps.explain: Voluntary pregnancy termination before full term is MTP, done about 45-50 million times a year worldwide, a fifth of all conceptions.
First-trimester terminations up to twelve weeks are relatively safe; second-trimester ones carry far greater risk.

Legalised in 1971, refined by the 2017 amendment: within twelve weeks one registered practitioner's opinion suffices; from over twelve up to twenty-four weeks, two must agree in good faith that continuing threatens the woman's life or health or that the child would be seriously handicapped.
Illegal abortions by unqualified hands can be fatal, and sex-selective termination after amniocentesis is unlawful; counselling and better facilities are the antidotes.

concepts.title: Sexually Transmitted Infections: Curable, Incurable, Prevention
concepts.definition: Infections passed through intercourse -- genital herpes, chlamydiasis, gonorrhoea, syphilis, genital warts, trichomoniasis, hepatitis-B and HIV leading to AIDS -- are mostly curable when caught early, but hepatitis-B, genital herpes and HIV have no complete cure, and cases peak in the 15-24 age band.
concepts.key_idea: Early symptoms are slight or absent, especially in women, so delay lets infections escalate into pelvic inflammatory disease, ectopic pregnancy, still birth, infertility or cancers.
question_patterns: list the common sexually transmitted infections and separate the curable from the incurable
why do STIs often go undetected in infected women
which complications follow untreated reproductive tract infections
other than intercourse how can hepatitis B and HIV spread
state three simple rules that protect against contracting an STI
which age group reports the highest STI incidence and why is that worrying

solution_steps.explain: Gonorrhoea, syphilis, genital herpes, chlamydiasis, genital warts, trichomoniasis, hepatitis-B and HIV are the headline STIs, also called VD or RTIs.
All but hepatitis-B, genital herpes and HIV clear up with early, proper treatment; those three can also travel by shared needles, surgical instruments, transfused blood or from mother to foetus.

Itching, fluid discharge, mild pain or swelling are easy to ignore, infected women may show nothing at all, and stigma delays testing until PID, abortions, still births, ectopic pregnancies, infertility or tract cancers appear.
Avoid sex with unknown or multiple partners, use condoms every time, and consult a qualified doctor at once for testing and full treatment when in doubt.

concepts.title: Infertility and Assisted Reproductive Technologies
concepts.definition: Couples unable to conceive despite unprotected cohabitation -- for physical, congenital, disease, drug, immunological or psychological reasons, and often on the male side -- can turn to ART: IVF with embryo transfer, ZIFT or IUT by embryo stage, GIFT with a donor ovum, ICSI sperm injection, artificial insemination, or legal adoption.
concepts.key_idea: Embryos of up to eight blastomeres go into the fallopian tube (ZIFT), older ones into the uterus (IUT), and donor-egg GIFT serves women who ovulate poorly but can carry a pregnancy.
question_patterns: define infertility and list the possible causes behind a childless couple
differentiate ZIFT from IUT on the basis of embryo stage
what happens in ICSI and which infertility problem does it answer
how does artificial insemination help when the male partner cannot inseminate
when is GIFT the suitable assisted reproductive choice
why is adoption described as one of the best routes to parenthood in India

solution_steps.explain: Infertility means no children despite unprotected co-habitation, with causes spread across both partners -- the blame-the-woman reflex is usually wrong, since the male factor is frequent.

IVF joins collected ova and sperms in the lab; the zygote or early embryo of at most eight blastomeres transfers into the fallopian tube (ZIFT), while beyond eight blastomeres it goes into the uterus (IUT).

GIFT places a donor's ovum into another woman's tube; ICSI injects a single sperm straight into the ovum; AI introduces husband's or donor's semen into vagina or uterus (IUI) for low sperm counts or insemination failure.
These techniques demand costly instruments and expert hands, so access is limited and emotionally loaded, which is why legal adoption remains a humane, widely available answer.

worked_examples.source_ref: lebo103.txt lines 107-122 (population figures and 2011 census growth rate)
worked_examples.question_pattern: A country holds {current_population} billion people and its population grows at {annual_growth} per year. What population does that rate predict after {years} years?

solution_template.explain: One plus the growth rate gives the factor each year multiplies by: 1 + 0.02 = 1.02.
Raise the factor to the year count and multiply: 1.2 * 1.02**3 is about 1.273 billion.
The compounded figure is the expected head count after the given span.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A gynaecologist offers a patient a copper releasing device and a hormone releasing device as choices. Explain how each prevents pregnancy and what both share in common.

solution_template.explain: Both IUD types raise phagocytosis of sperms inside the uterus.
Copper ions from CuT, Cu7 or Multiload 375 suppress sperm motility and fertilising capacity.
Progestasert or LNG-20 additionally makes the uterus unfit for implantation and the cervix hostile to sperms.

worked_examples.source_ref: lebo103.txt lines 380-397 (IVF, ZIFT, IUT, GIFT, ICSI passages)
worked_examples.question_pattern: An IVF lab holds one embryo with six blastomeres and another with sixteen. State the transfer site and technique name for each.

solution_template.explain: Up to eight blastomeres means a very early embryo: it goes into the fallopian tube by ZIFT.
Beyond eight blastomeres the embryo must go into the uterus by IUT.
Each transfer site mimics where the embryo of that stage would naturally be travelling in the female tract.

worked_examples.source_ref: lebo103.txt lines 253-321 (MTP section with amendment act box)
worked_examples.question_pattern: A pregnancy has run fifteen weeks and the woman seeks termination on health grounds. How many registered medical practitioners must certify it, and up to what week count does this rule apply?

solution_template.explain: Fifteen weeks falls in the band above twelve but below twenty-four weeks.
Two registered medical practitioners must form the opinion in good faith that a permitted ground exists.
Within the first twelve weeks a single registered practitioner's opinion is enough.
